answer: Elastic Overlap Dividend. Each identity earns a dividend only where its activity overlaps with a random sample of neighbors, weighted by a slowly diffusing trust field that erodes like shale under repeated re-registration. An attacker must sustain dense cross-links across sampled regions; sparse sybil clusters fail to overlap and earn zero, and re-registering resets a karst-like sinkhole of decayed dividend history. Each attempted clone costs the full operating overhead of a distinct active profile, since the dividend river flows only through verified overlap, never to isolated nodes.
